Ride-Hailing Company Grab Lifts 2026 Guidance On Improving Profitability
By Kimberley Kao and P.R. Venkat
Southeast Asian ride-hailing and delivery specialist Grab reported strong earnings in the third quarter, and raised its full-year guidance as its core businesses become more profitable as they grow.
The Nasdaq-listed company on Tuesday said its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rose 73% to a record $237 million for the three months ended September.
Net profit was $18 million, up from $17 million a year earlier, as a sharp rise in operating profit was largely offset by losses on its investments.

Revenue rose a stronger-than-expected 27% to $1.112 billion, driven by growth across all its core segments, including on-demand services and financial services. Visible Alpha consensus had forecast $1.08 billion.
Grab raised its annual adjusted Ebitda forecast to between $790 million and $800 million, from $720 million to $740 million previously, citing improving profitability across its core businesses.
The metric excludes restructuring costs, share-based compensation expenses, fair-value changes on investments and other expenses.
It also raised its revenue guidance for 2026 to $4.15 billion to $4.20 billion, from $4.10 billion to $4.15 billion.
